title: Related-Key Security for Derived-Key XOR-Cascades
summary: Ideal-cipher security for the derived-key XOR-cascade relies on independent per-key permutations; whether a practical instantiation has the needed related-key security remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Consider an XOR-cascade whose distinct encryption keys are derived deterministically from a single key. Its ideal-cipher security relies on the modeled independence of the permutations associated with different keys, an assumption that does not by itself justify a practical block-cipher instantiation. Determine whether such an instantiation provides the required form of security under related-key attack; alternatively, use independent keys for the encryption steps to retain the same security statement at the cost of additional key material.

scope.domain: Related-key security of block-cipher key-length extension using XOR-cascades.
assumptions: Ideal-cipher model — permutations associated with different keys are modeled as independent.
parameters: Key-scheduling choice — derive distinct encryption-step keys deterministically from one key, or use independent keys at greater key-material cost
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether a practical block-cipher instantiation of the derived-key XOR-cascade provides the required related-key security.

citations.label: Plain versus Randomized Cascading-Based Key-Length Extension for Block Ciphers

progress.summary: The source presents the derived-key cascade as safe in the ideal-cipher model while identifying related-key security as necessary for a practical instantiation. It notes that independent encryption-step keys retain the security statement but require more key material.
citation_labels: Peter Gazi et al., Plain versus Randomized Cascading-Based Key-Length Extension for Block Ciphers
